name: DaVinci Cut Page Speed And Sync Bin Multicam
use_when: A simple assembly needs speed more than detailed layered timeline control.
A vlog, event, meeting, news, or rough cut uses many clips that can be browsed as a source tape.
Multiple cameras can be synced by audio and used as quick cutaways.
avoid_when: The sequence needs detailed audio layering, narrative trimming, or complex track control.
The editor expects every edit to happen exactly at the playhead instead of the nearest edit point.
The multicam sources do not share usable sync reference.

timeline_pattern.source_tape_rule: Use Source Tape to skim all clips in a bin as one continuous browsing surface.
timeline_pattern.smart_insert_rule: Smart Insert targets the nearest edit point/edit indicator, so confirm placement after use.
timeline_pattern.sync_bin_rule: Sync camera angles by audio, save sync, then use angle picks to place cutaways over a base clip.
timeline_pattern.page_choice_rule: Use Edit page when the cut grows beyond fast assembly.

motion.rule: Cut page transitions and simple reframes should stay secondary to speed and clarity.

sound.rule: After Sync Bin angle insertion, check that the chosen audio source remains intentional and does not double or phase.

captions.rule: Generate captions after the multicam timing is stable enough that angle insertions will not churn caption timing.

color.rule: Expect multicam angles to need shot matching later in Color.

implementation.ffmpeg: Use synced multi-source ranges and an angle decision list; render cutaway tests after alignment.
implementation.remotion: Represent synced cameras as angle tracks with shared master time and visible angle ranges.
implementation.blender: Use synchronized VSE strips and markers when cutting between rendered camera views.
implementation.capcut_equivalent: Use batch-selected clips, audio sync if available, and manual upper-track cutaways over a base angle.
implementation.premiere_equivalent: Use multicam source sequences, source monitor angle switching, insert/overwrite edits, and a detailed sequence for final trim.

common_mistakes: Using Cut page speed for a sequence that needs careful audio/story control.
Trusting Smart Insert without checking the actual edit point.
Placing multicam angles without checking sync and audio source.
Leaving fast rough-cut transitions in a final narrative sequence by accident.
qc: Is Cut page the right tool for this sequence complexity?
Did Smart Insert land at the intended edit point?
Are Sync Bin angles correctly synced and visible at the chosen moment?
Does the final audio source remain clean after angle changes?
Was the sequence moved to Edit page review before detailed finishing?
